about: The ground the Battle of Verdun was fought over, 21 February to December 1916, in Lambert-93 metres (EPSG:2154): from the German first line of 21 February to the furthest the Germans came, both banks of the Meuse. The editor draws it as the battle's outline: the traced ground taken out 500 m and smoothed, so every traced line lies at least 400 m inside it.
definition: North: the German first line on 21 February (left bank from the 6 March map, carte n° 19, where it stood until the attack of that day; right bank from carte n° 14). South: on the left bank the French first line of 20 June (carte n° 9), after Côte 304, the Mort-Homme and Cumières had fallen; on the right bank the German first line of April (carte n° 24), pushed out round Fleury by the German front of 10 July and the French line on the evening of 12 July (carte n° 11), the furthest the Germans came towards Souville. Between the banks, the Meuse. East: straight across the Woëvre plain from Gincrey to Châtillon-sous-les-Côtes, abandoned by the French on 24 and 25 February; that edge is approximate, the line there not being on any 1916 sheet we have. Lines traced from each sheet's printed ink by scripts/trace-front-line.py, through its kilometre grid; the left bank's French line and the 12 July line along waypoints read by eye. The outline is good to some tens of metres where traced; the Woëvre edge to a kilometre or so.
checked: Haumont, Samogneux, Beaumont, Louvemont, Ornes, Bezonvaux, Douaumont, Fleury, Vaux, Cumières, Béthincourt, Malancourt, Haucourt, Forges, Regnéville, Champneuville, Mogeville, Maucourt and Dieppe, all taken by the Germans in 1916, lie inside; Verdun, Esnes, Chattancourt, Marre, Charny, Bras, Belleville, Avocourt, Moulainville and Eix, held by the French throughout, and Consenvoye, Flabas, Azannes, Gremilly, Montfaucon, Cuisy and Étain, behind the German lines, lie outside. Damloup's present-day centre falls 200 m outside: the village was rebuilt north-east of the one destroyed, which lies inside.
